wetlandDistribution.metaTitle: Global wetland distribution — Youth Wetland Research Platform
wetlandDistribution.title: Explore world wetlands from your screen
wetlandDistribution.lead: This overview summarizes major spatial patterns and regional contrasts. Figures draw on public literature and global compilations—for education and outreach, not operational decisions.
wetlandDistribution.introBody: Wetlands are unevenly spread: cold, wet high latitudes; tropical coasts and large river basins; and inland floodplains each form distinct clusters. Climate, terrain, and hydrology together shape these macro-scale maps.

regions.title: High latitudes & boreal peatlands
regions.body: Canada, Russia, and Nordic countries hold vast boreal peatlands and tundra wetlands—major soil carbon stores and breeding grounds for migratory birds.

regions.title: Tropical & subtropical coasts
regions.body: Mangroves, seagrass beds, and deltas concentrate along Southeast Asia, South Asia, and tropical Americas, supporting exceptional biodiversity.

regions.title: Inland rivers & floodplains
regions.body: Amazon, Congo, Mississippi, and similar basins form ribbon-like floodplain wetlands that buffer floods and sustain migratory species.

wetlandDistribution.chinaBody: China’s wetlands total roughly 56.35 million hectares—first in Asia. Asia holds about one-third of the world’s mapped wetland area, with North America next; exact shares vary by definition, year, and dataset—always check primary sources when citing.
tips: Pair global maps with national protected-area networks and conventions (e.g., Ramsar) to connect “where” with “how we govern.”
Compare satellite products with field surveys—national totals and global grids may disagree at margins.
Track peatlands and coastal wetlands when linking to climate goals and nature-based solutions.
